subject: Hosted API response-time cliff — immediate mitigation & next steps
messages:
From: Jessica Tan <jessica.tan@acme-logistics.com>
To: rachel.kim@redwood.com
Cc: ops@acme-logistics.com
Date: 2026-09-12T13:22:00-04:00
Subject: Re: sudden p99 spikes impacting order-processing pipelines

Rachel —

We started seeing elevated p99 latency and a ~3x drop in throughput to your Hosted API at ~12:45pm ET. This is causing timeouts for our order batch jobs (we're seeing 504s). Our SLAs are being hit and customers are noticing delays.

Attached is a Grafana snapshot from our side showing the p95/p99 climb. Can you confirm this is on your side and what immediate mitigation you can take?

We rely on your hosted endpoint for synchronous scoring in our fulfillment flow — this is high severity for us.

Thanks,
Jessica Tan
Lead SRE, Acme Logistics
From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
To: Jessica Tan <jessica.tan@acme-logistics.com>
Cc: sean.gallagher@redwood.com, dev.patel@redwood.com, hannah.schmitt@redwood.com
Date: 2026-09-12T13:30:00-04:00
Subject: Re: sudden p99 spikes impacting order-processing pipelines

Thanks for the flag, Jessica — and apologies for the disruption. We’re treating this as a Sev-1. I’ve looped in SRE and runtime leads (Sean, Dev) and we’re triaging now.

Immediate plan:
- SRE will validate host-side metrics and queue depth.
- If backlog is confirmed, we will temporarily change batching parameters and scale serving workers to reduce tail latency.
- I’ll update you within 30 minutes with mitigation and ETA for full recovery.

Please leave the traces/attachments you already captured — they help a lot.

–Rachel Kim
Enterprise AE, Redwood Inference
Rachel.Kim@redwood.com
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
To: rachel.kim@redwood.com, dev.patel@redwood.com
Cc: hannah.schmitt@redwood.com
Date: 2026-09-12T13:45:00-04:00
Subject: Re: sudden p99 spikes impacting order-processing pipelines

Quick triage update (what I see from the control plane):
- Time window: 12:42–13:20 ET shows a sharp rise in queue depth on the hosted inference cluster serving the default route (route-id: hosted-default-us).
- Symptoms: sustained per-host request backlog -> increased batch assembly wait times -> p95/p99 latency regressions. Error rate (5xx) uptick correlates with the queue drain timeouts.
- Recent change: autoscaling policy rolled out yesterday increased max_batch_timeout from 80ms -> 200ms to favor throughput; combined with a spike of large-token requests we’re seeing blocks building up.

Immediate mitigations (executed or in progress):
1) Reduced max_batch_size from 64 -> 16 (hotfix applied at 13:32 ET).
2) Reduced max_batch_timeout from 200ms -> 60ms (applied at 13:34 ET) so batches don't wait behind long requests.
3) Scaled up worker pool for the affected pool by 2x (rolling instances added starting 13:35 ET).
4) Enabled conservative prefix/KV cache for common prompt prefixes used by Acme (dev note: this should reduce tokenization/kv hit latency).

Expected effect: queue depth should begin to fall within 5–11 minutes of changes; p99 should start improving shortly thereafter. We will keep collecting heap/CPU/GPU utilization and tail latencies.

Attachments: snippet of API server log showing backlog counters (api_server_logs_excerpt.txt).

—Sean (SRE)
From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
To: Jessica Tan <jessica.tan@acme-logistics.com>
Cc: sean.gallagher@redwood.com, dev.patel@redwood.com, hannah.schmitt@redwood.com, laura.bennett@redwood.com
Date: 2026-09-12T14:00:00-04:00
Subject: Re: sudden p99 spikes impacting order-processing pipelines

Jessica —

Sean applied mitigations (batch size/timeouts lowered, worker pool increased, cache enabled). We are already seeing the queue_depth metric drop and p99 trending down in our dashboards — attached is our Grafana snapshot (grafana_p99_spike_20260912.png).

Action items and timeline:
- Short term: Keep the conservative batching/timeouts for the next 6 hours while we validate across traffic shapes.
- Postmortem: SRE will produce a root cause analysis by EOD tomorrow and include corrective actions (better rollout guardrails for batching policy changes).
- Credits/SLA: I’ve escalated to Hannah and Laura to discuss contractual remedies — we’ll confirm next steps within 24 hours.

Thanks for the quick reporting and traces — that made triage faster. Please confirm if your traffic is back to normal on your side.

Best,
Rachel
Enterprise AE, Redwood Inference
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>

Laura — recommend we offer a single-billing-period credit proportional to observed downtime plus waive one-month overage charges for their August usage as a gesture (we can finalize numbers with finance). Thoughts?

—Hannah

Regards,
Jessica
